messages:
maya: Heads-up from onboarding 'tengu-lite' quantized int8. Latency and throughput look good, but our locale smoke surfaced two regressions: (1) JP vertical annotations (ruby markers) occasionally omitted, (2) Hebrew output from en->he sometimes places angle brackets <> around names in reversed positions.

li: can you share the exact eval run and quant config?

maya: eval: `./smoke_run --model tengu-lite --quant int8_packed_v2 --suites jp_vertical,he_translation --seed 1234 --decoding topk=50,temp=0.7` runtime had KV cache and batching enabled.

noah: any token/id diffs vs fp16 baseline? small repro helps.

maya: pasted a short repro. baseline vs tengu-int8 token codepoints for en->he sample:
```
# src en: "Call <Anna> soon."
# baseline codepoints: [0x05D0,0x05D1,0x0020,0x003C,0x0041,0x006E,0x006E,0x0061,0x003E,0x0020,0x0073,0x006F,0x006F,0x006E,0x002E]
# tengu-int8 codepoints: [0x05D0,0x05D1,0x0020,0x003E,0x0041,0x006E,0x006E,0x0061,0x003C,0x0020,0x0073,0x006F,0x006F,0x006E,0x002E]
```
angle brackets appear swapped in token stream (positions 4 and 9).

li: interesting. if the token stream itself reordered, it's happening during decode not detok. does disabling kv-cache change result?

maya: yes — `--runtime no-kvcache` yields baseline ordering. With kv-cache enabled the swap is deterministic for sequences with seq_len >= 80; shorter contexts unaffected. Batching changes nothing.

noah: that points to a vectorized kv pack/unpack issue for larger seqs. I'll instrument the pack offsets in the packer code and run small loop reproducer. Could also be a signed/unsigned index overflow in stride calc.

maya: on JP vertical suite a different failure: ruby markers U+FFF9..U+FFFB present in baseline but missing intermittently in int8. Example tokens:
```
# vertical sample: kanji plus marker
# baseline contains marker indexes: [0x6F22,0x5B57,0xFFF9,0x0072,0x0075,0x0062,0x0079,0xFFFB]
# tengu-int8 result: [0x6F22,0x5B57]
```
so marker region dropped entirely; hit-rate collapsed from 97.5% to 58.2% on suite.

li: do you have logits/prob snapshot for those marker tokens? if int8 quant pushes them low they get pruned by topk sampling. try `--dump-logits --topk 200` for a couple samples.

maya: single-step logits show big shift. baseline marker logit ~ -1.6 (prob ~0.17), int8 logit ~ -6.0 (prob ~0.002).

noah: run `--force-quant-calib --calib-samples 2000` and also try `--precision-exempt 0xFFF0-0xFFFF` to compute logits for marker ranges in fp16. If that recovers markers, it's quant rounding error.

kernel-team-bot: created issue KERNEL-4012 "tengu-lite int8: kv-pack stride overflow causing token reorder at seq>=80" assigned to @noah, due 2025-01-18.

qa-bot: created eval EVAL-9001 linking logs s3://redwood-evals/tengu-lite/int8/1756601234/; includes sample ids and seeded runs.

li: next steps: (1) noah to produce minimal C reproducer for kv-pack stride and bisect kernel commits; (2) I'll run forced-calib + precision-exempt experiments and report marker keep-rate; (3) maya to mark he bracket reorder as P0 for customer-impact. Triage 9:30am PT tomorrow.

maya: adding failing sample ids to KERNEL-4012 and uploading tarball. thanks all.
